title_en: Xixia Longcheng Special Materials Co., Ltd. v. Yulin Intellectual Property Office and Shaanxi Coal and Chemical Industry Group Shenmu Tianyuan Chemical Co., Ltd. — administrative handling dispute over patent infringement
ruling_gist_en: 1. Where a member of a collegial panel who has been explicitly substituted nonetheless signs the administrative decision under review, this effectively constitutes 'the adjudicator did not adjudicate, and the adjudicator did not adjudicate,' which deviates from the principle of administration according to law and undermines public trust in administrative enforcement authorities. full_text_en:
Xixia Longcheng Special Materials Co., Ltd. v. Yulin City Intellectual Property Office and Shaanxi Coal and Chemical Industry Group Shenmu Tianyuan Chemical Co., Ltd.

— Administrative dispute over patent infringement

Ruling Summary

1. Where a panel member who has been expressly replaced nonetheless signs the administrative decision under challenge, this effectively constitutes "the adjudicator did not rule, and the ruling was not made by the adjudicator," which deviates from the principle of law-based administration and undermines public trust in administrative enforcement entities. Such conduct constitutes a serious violation of statutory procedures. This finding is not affected by the subjective awareness of the administrative counterparty, nor is it altered by the administrative counterparty's failure to object. It does not fall within the circumstances of "minor procedural violation of an administrative act without the need to revoke the administrative act."

2. That administrative enforcement personnel possess the requisite enforcement qualifications is an inherent element of the legality of an administrative body's status and an inevitable requirement for comprehensively advancing law-based administration. In principle, the collegial panel that renders an administrative decision under challenge should be composed of staff members of the administrative body who are qualified for patent administrative enforcement. Even when enforcement personnel are dispatched from other localities, formal and complete official procedures must be followed.

3. The content of the patent claims is the sole criterion for delineating the scope of patent protection; the description and drawings are only used to interpret the content of the claims. When interpreting the claims using the description and drawings, the specific descriptions of particular embodiments in the description must not be read into the claims.

Administrative Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2017) Zui Gao Fa Xing Zai No. 84

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Xixia Longcheng Special Materials Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 88, North Section of Gongye Avenue, Xixia County, Nanyang City, Henan Province (West Side of North Section of National Highway 311).

Legal Representative: Zhu Shucheng, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yang Cunji, Attorney at Beijing Zhihui Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ji Fajun, male, born April 10, 1979, Han ethnicity, patent agent of Zhengzhou Zhiji Intellectual Property Agency Co., Ltd., domiciled in Nanyang City, Henan Province.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Yulin City Intellectual Property Office. Domicile: No. 35, Changle Road, Yuyang District, Yulin City, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Hao Kanglin, Director of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Weiliang, Section Chief of the Office.

Agent ad litem: Gou Hongdong, male, born December 6, 1965, Han ethnicity, Deputy Director of Baoji City Intellectual Property Office, domiciled in Baoji City, Shaanxi Province.

Respondent (Third Party at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Shaanxi Coal and Chemical Industry Group Shenmu Tianyuan Chemical Co., Ltd. Domicile: Jinjie Industrial Park, Shenmu County, Yulin City, Shaanxi Province.

Legal Representative: Mao Shiqiang, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Li Xiangdong, Attorney at Beijing Hengdu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Yuan, Intern Attorney at Beijing Hengdu Law Firm.

The applicant for retrial, Xixia Longcheng Special Materials Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xixia Company), dissatisfied with the administrative judgment (2016) Shan Xing Zhong No. 94 rendered by the Shaanxi High People's Court in the case regarding the administrative handling of a patent infringement dispute with the respondents Yulin City Intellectual Property Office (hereinafter referred to as Yulin Office) and Shaanxi Coal and Chemical Industry Group Shenmu Tianyuan Chemical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianyuan Company), filed an application for retrial with this Court. On September 21, 2017, this Court ruled to grant the retrial and take cognizance of the case. After the retrial was granted, this Court formed a collegial panel according to law and held a public hearing on December 15, 2017. The agents ad litem of Xixia Company, Yang Cunji and Ji Fajun; the agents ad litem of Yulin Office, Zhang Weiliang and Gou Hongdong; and the agents ad litem of Tianyuan Company, Li Xiangdong and Li Yuan, attended the proceedings. The trial of this case is now concluded.

On June 10, 2015, Xixia Company requested administrative handling from the Yulin Office, alleging that the equipment for coal classification and conversion manufactured and used by Tianyuan Company infringed its utility model patent right No. ZL201020586802.2 for an "Internal Heat External Heat Type Coal Material Decomposition Device" (hereinafter referred to as the patent-in-suit), and requesting that Tianyuan Company be ordered to cease the aforementioned infringing activities.

The Yulin Office held that Xixia Company determined the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit based on Claim 1 of the said patent. Because the accused infringing equipment was bulky and was in production use, its internal structure could not be observed through disassembly. Therefore, the technical features of the accused infringing equipment were determined based on photographs and a simplified structural diagram of the accused infringing equipment provided by Tianyuan Company and acknowledged by Xixia Company. Upon comparison, the sealed kiln body of the patent-in-suit differed in structure, function, and effect from the jacket of the accused infringing equipment and did not constitute an equivalent feature. The coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline of the patent-in-suit differed in structure and working principle from the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing equipment and was also not equivalent. The coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline of the patent-in-suit was located within the sealed kiln body and completely enclosed; the two could not rotate relative to each other. The rotary kiln body of the accused infringing equipment was not located inside the jacket; the two could rotate relative to each other. The kiln body of the patent-in-suit had good sealing properties, improving heat transfer efficiency. The accused infringing equipment had three relatively independent heating jackets set on the outer wall of the rotary kiln body, completely isolating the heat supply from the pyrolysis process, improving safety. The technical effects and objectives of the two were different. Therefore, the accused infringing equipment did not fall within the scope of protection of the patent and did not constitute infringement of the patent-in-suit. Furthermore, Tianyuan Company explicitly did not assert prior art defense during the oral hearing. On September 1, 2015, the Yulin Office issued the "Decision on Handling a Patent Infringement Dispute" Yu Zhi Fa Chu Zi [2015] No. 9 (hereinafter referred to as the Administrative Decision under Challenge), rejecting Xixia Company's request that Tianyuan Company be ordered to cease the patent infringing activities.

Dissatisfied with the Administrative Decision under Challenge, Xixia Company initiated proceedings before the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province.

Xixia Company alleged: 1. The jacket of the accused infringing equipment was formed by riveting three steel plates together. The jacket was arranged circumferentially around the kiln body. The jacket and the kiln body were sealed and fixed to form a sealed container. High-temperature gas was introduced into the sealed container to heat the coal powder inside the kiln body. The jacket was not an independent structure used alone but had to be used in conjunction with the kiln body. However, Claim 1 did not limit the specific structure of the kiln body; it could be square, round, irregularly shaped, or even a jacket structure. As long as it constituted a sealed container, it was equivalent to the sealed kiln body of Claim 1. 2. The accused infringing equipment adopted a three-section structure. Regardless of how many jackets the accused infringing equipment had, its essence was that a kiln body was arranged within the jacket, high-temperature gas was introduced into the sealed container formed by the jacket and the kiln body, and coal was introduced into the kiln body. Claim 1 did not limit the number of sealed kiln bodies. 3. The rotary kiln body of the accused infringing equipment was equivalent to the coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline of the patent-in-suit. The technical means (kiln body), the function performed (introducing coal powder), and the effect achieved (fully heating the coal powder within the kiln body, raising the temperature to decompose and produce gas, tar gas, and coal) employed by the accused infringing equipment were equivalent to the means, function, and effect of the patent-in-suit. 4. The three-section jacket of the accused infringing equipment wrapped around the kiln body, changing the full wrapping of the coal material decomposition propulsion channel by the kiln body of the patent-in-suit into the partial wrapping of the kiln body by the three-section jacket of the accused infringing equipment. This sacrificed some heat energy and reduced heat exchange efficiency. The improvement on the technical solution of the patent-in-suit should fall within the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit. In conclusion, the Yulin Office's determination that Tianyuan Company did not constitute patent infringement was erroneous. Xixia Company requested the court to annul the Administrative Decision under Challenge according to law and that Yulin Office bear the litigation costs of this case.

Yulin Office argued: 1. The jacket of the accused infringing equipment was itself fixed and wrapped around the rotary kiln body and did not rotate; only the rotary kiln body rotated relative to the jacket. The jacket did not completely enclose the rotary kiln body to form a sealed container. In contrast, the sealed kiln body of the patent-in-suit was a sealed container and was fixed relative to the coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline. It rotated itself and drove the internal coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline to rotate, causing the material to move and advance. The sealed kiln body and the coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline could not rotate relative to each other. Therefore, the jacket of the accused infringing equipment was neither identical nor equivalent to the sealed kiln body of the patent-in-suit. 2. Although the heat exchange space of the accused infringing equipment and the heat exchange chamber of the patent-in-suit both served the function of containing hot air to heat the coal material for decomposition, the heat exchange chamber of the patent-in-suit was a continuous space between the coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline and the inner wall of the sealed kiln body, aimed at improving heat transfer efficiency. In contrast, for the convenience of equipment manufacturing and the safety of the pyrolysis process, the heat exchange space of the accused infringing equipment was composed of three discontinuous spaces between the rotary kiln body and the three jackets, improving the safety of equipment operation. Therefore, the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing equipment was neither identical nor equivalent to the coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline of the patent-in-suit. In conclusion, the accused infringing equipment did not fall within the scope of protection of the patent and did not constitute infringement of the patent-in-suit. The facts found in the Administrative Decision under Challenge were clear and the evidence sufficient. Yulin Office requested that Xixia Company's claim be dismissed.

Tianyuan Company submitted: 1. The jacket of the accused infringing equipment was a hollow sleeve surrounding the rotary kiln body and was non-sealed, whereas the kiln body of the patent-in-suit was a sealed structure. The heat exchange efficiency of the jacket was lower than that of the sealed kiln body; it sacrificed heat exchange efficiency to simplify the equipment structure and reduce the risk of explosion. The two differed in technical means and effect and did not constitute equivalent features. The accused infringing equipment lacked the feature of "a coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline arranged within the kiln body" of the patent-in-suit. The jacket only served as a heating sleeve placed over the outer wall of the kiln body and did not have the closed sealed structure of the patent-in-suit. The rotary kiln was not located inside the outer jacket; the overall structure of the rotary kiln was larger than the outer jacket, making it impossible to arrange the rotary kiln inside the outer jacket. The accused infringing equipment did not have a structure as round and slender as the pipeline of the patent-in-suit. The rotary kiln body rotated relative to a jacket that partially wrapped it, whereas the coal material decomposition propulsion pipeline of the patent-in-suit was completely sealed within the kiln body, and its method of operation was not specified; the technical effects of the two were different. 2. The accused infringing technical solution constituted prior art. Therefore, Tianyuan Company did not constitute infringement of the patent-in-suit. The procedure for the Administrative Decision under Challenge was lawful, and the application of law was correct. Tianyuan Company requested that the decision be upheld.

After trial, the court of first instance found the following facts: On October 26, 2010, Xixia Company filed an application with the State Intellectual Property Office for a utility model patent named "Internal Heat External Heat Type Coal Material Decomposition Device." The patent was granted on May 11, 2011, with the patent number ZL201020586802.2. In this case, Xixia Company explicitly stated that it sought protection for Claim 1, the content of which is: An internal heat external heat type coal material decomposition device, comprising a sealed kiln body, characterized in that: a coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline is arranged within the kiln body; the coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline is provided with a coal inlet, a coal outlet, and a decomposition gas collection pipe; a heat exchange chamber is arranged between the coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline and the inner wall of the kiln body; the heat exchange chamber is in communication with a high-temperature gas heating mechanism; and the heat exchange chamber is provided with a heating gas outlet pipe. On January 4, 2014, the State Intellectual Property Office issued an evaluation report on the utility model patent right. The preliminary conclusion was that for all claims of the patent-in-suit, no defects were found that would not meet the conditions for granting the patent right.

On July 2, 2015, the Nanyang City Zhisheng Notary Office of Henan Province issued Notarial Certificate [(2015) Nan Zhi Zheng Min Zi No. 1893], which recorded: Entering http://www.tvci.com.cn/SHowNews.asp?id=8705 for Shaanxi Coal and Chemical Industry Group Shenmu Tianyuan Chemical Co., Ltd. in the 360 navigation bar; the page accessed was for Shaanxi Coal and Chemical Industry Group Shenmu Tianyuan Chemical Co., Ltd., with content stating that the company's low-rank pulverized coal rotary pyrolysis technology for producing anthracite passed the scientific and technological achievement appraisal. The design achievement was used by Tianyuan Company. The main technical features of the low-rank pulverized coal rotary pyrolysis anthracite production device included: (1) a rotary kiln body; (2) three jackets respectively located on the outer wall of the rotary kiln body, the rotary kiln body being rotatable relative to the jackets; (3) a heating mechanism; (4) a coal inlet, a coal outlet, and a heating gas outlet pipe; (5) a heat exchange space between the rotary kiln body and the jackets; (6) the heat exchange space heating the coal material within the rotary kiln body for decomposition.

After comparing the technical features recorded in Claim 1 of the patent-in-suit with the technical features of the accused infringing equipment, Xixia Company raised no objection to the Yulin Office's finding that both had a heating mechanism, a coal inlet, a coal outlet, a heating gas outlet pipe, and a heat exchange chamber between the rotary kiln body and the jacket. However, Xixia Company objected to the Yulin Office's finding that the sealed kiln body of the patent-in-suit and the jacket of the accused infringing equipment, as well as the coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline of the patent-in-suit and the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing equipment, were not identical.

During the trial of the first instance, Xixia Company stated: The collegial panel for the Administrative Decision under Challenge included Gou Hongdong, but Gou Hongdong, as Deputy Director of the Baoji City Intellectual Property Office, could not participate in the handling of the patent infringement dispute in question. Xixia Company was unclear whether the Yulin Office had informed the parties of the composition of the collegial panel and had not filed an application for withdrawal. The drawings and the actual equipment of the accused infringing equipment had consistent technical features; an on-site comparison was unnecessary.

The Yulin Office stated: Due to the significant nature of this case and a shortage of existing personnel, after consulting the superior competent department, it was ultimately decided that Gou Hongdong and others would form a collegial panel with Yulin Office staff. The specific identities of the collegial panel members were disclosed to the parties during the first oral hearing, and Xixia Company raised no objection. The dispute in question involved joint law enforcement at the provincial and municipal levels. Article 80 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China stipulates that higher-level departments provide operational guidance to lower-level departments. This guidance includes the deployment of personnel for law enforcement within the province, and administrative agencies typically deploy personnel amongst themselves in practice. The Yulin Office had consulted the State Intellectual Property Office through the Shaanxi Provincial Intellectual Property Office. The State Intellectual Property Office replied by letter that, given the current imbalance in the number and capability of law enforcement personnel across the national intellectual property system, the State Intellectual Property Office is promoting a law enforcement collaboration and dispatch mechanism throughout the system, including the dispatch of personnel and case assignments, which constitutes an internal administrative matter.

Tianyuan Company stated: Before the oral hearing, the Yulin Office had issued notices to both Tianyuan Company and Xixia Company, and neither party raised any objection to the identities of the collegial panel members.

The court of first instance further found that the "Patent Administrative Enforcement Capability Enhancement Project Plan" formulated by the State Intellectual Property Office explicitly requires the establishment of a national and several regional patent administrative enforcement coordination and dispatch centers to improve the level and efficiency of law enforcement case coordination. Select regions were to carry out pilot projects, establishing several regional patent administrative enforcement coordination and dispatch centers; promoting the establishment of a national patent administrative enforcement command and dispatch center to accelerate the systematic and standardized realization of cross-regional law enforcement collaboration. In accordance with the requirements of the "Patent Administrative Enforcement Capability Enhancement Project Plan," the Shaanxi Provincial Intellectual Property Office carried out patent administrative enforcement coordination and dispatch work, deploying patent administrative enforcement personnel with rich practical experience in patent administrative enforcement and a high level of proficiency in implementing patent laws and regulations to participate in the trial of patent administrative cases across cities. The collegial panel members for the case in question, Gou Hongdong and Bai Long, were law enforcement personnel from the Baoji City Intellectual Property Office, dispatched by the Shaanxi Provincial Intellectual Property Office to the case collegial panel of the Yulin Office to carry out the administrative handling of the patent infringement dispute in question.

The court of first instance held:

1. Regarding whether the making of the Administrative Decision under Challenge violated statutory procedures.

Xixia Company argued that the following act of the Yulin Office violated statutory procedures: The collegial panel for the Administrative Decision under Challenge included Gou Hongdong, but Gou Hongdong was the Deputy Director of the Baoji City Intellectual Property Office and could not participate in the handling of the dispute in question. In this regard, considering that before the making of the Administrative Decision under Challenge, due to the significant nature of the case and a shortage of existing personnel, the Yulin Office, after consulting the superior competent department, ultimately decided that the Baoji City Intellectual Property Office would send personnel to participate and together form a collegial panel with Yulin Office staff; simultaneously, the Yulin Office had informed the parties of the collegial panel members during the oral hearing, and Xixia Company raised no objection; the Yulin Office had consulted the State Intellectual Property Office through the Shaanxi Provincial Intellectual Property Office, and the State Intellectual Property Office replied that, given the current imbalance in the number and capability of law enforcement personnel across the national intellectual property system, the State Intellectual Property Office is promoting a law enforcement collaboration and dispatch mechanism throughout the system, including the dispatch of personnel and case assignments, which constitutes an internal administrative matter, and carrying out law enforcement personnel dispatch work in accordance with current internal personnel regulations does not violate the internal exchange system. This demonstrates that the making of the Administrative Decision under Challenge did not violate statutory procedures.

2. Regarding whether the Administrative Decision under Challenge was based on conclusive evidence.

Due to the large size of the accused infringing equipment and its being in use, its internal structure could not be observed through disassembly. With the acknowledgment of Xixia Company, the Yulin Office used photographs and a simplified structural diagram of the accused infringing equipment to determine its technical features. Both Xixia Company and Tianyuan Company raised no objection to this. During the process of comparing technical features by the Yulin Office, Xixia Company and Tianyuan Company disputed whether the two groups of technical features – the sealed kiln body of the patent-in-suit versus the jacket of the accused infringing equipment, and the coal material propulsion decomposition pipeline of the patent-in-suit versus the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing equipment – constituted equivalents. There was no dispute regarding the remaining technical features. This demonstrates that the Administrative Decision under Challenge was based on conclusive evidence.

3. Regarding whether the application of law in the Administrative Decision under Challenge was correct.

(1) The accused infringing device and the patent in suit share the same subject matter, both being equipment for coal decomposition and utilization. Their technical features are: a rotary kiln body; three jackets respectively located on the outer wall of the rotary kiln body, with the rotary kiln body being rotatable relative to the jackets; a heating mechanism; a coal inlet, a coal outlet, and a heating gas outlet pipe; a heat exchange space between the rotary kiln body and the jackets; the heat exchange space heats the coal material inside the rotary kiln body for decomposition. The Yulin Bureau correctly identified the technical features of the accused infringing device. (2) The kiln body of the patent in suit refers to a complete spatial structure capable of containing other objects, whereas the jacket of the accused infringing device refers to equipment with a sleeve structure; the technical means of the two are different. Since the sealed kiln body of the patent in suit is a rotatable sealed container and does not have the technical features of a jacket, while the accused infringing device is equipped with jackets, with three jackets respectively fixed to the outer wall of the rotary kiln body, and the rotary kiln body rotates relative to the jackets, the functions of the two are different. The heat exchange efficiency of the jackets used in the accused infringing device is far lower than that of the sealed kiln body of the patent in suit, so the effects of the two are different. Therefore, the sealed kiln body of the patent in suit and the jackets of the accused infringing device do not constitute equivalent features. Xixia argued that Claim 1 does not limit the specific structure or number of kiln bodies, and that as long as the accused infringing device constitutes a sealed container, it is equivalent to the sealed kiln body in Claim 1. This argument is inconsistent with the facts and is not adopted. (3) The coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit refers to a round, slender, and hollow structure, whereas the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing device does not have a round, slender structure; the technical means of the two are different. The coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit is located inside its sealed kiln body, relying on a large amount of high-temperature gas inside the sealed kiln body to surround the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe for pyrolysis. The rotary kiln body of the accused infringing device has three jackets, and the rotary kiln body rotates relative to the jackets; the functions of the two are different. The coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit has the effect of preventing heat loss and improving heat transfer efficiency, while the rotary kiln body sacrifices heat exchange efficiency to simplify the equipment structure and reduce the risk of explosion; the effects of the two are different. Therefore, the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit and the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing device do not constitute equivalent features.

The court of first instance held that the facts found in the administrative decision were clear, the evidence was conclusive, the application of law was correct, and the procedure was lawful. On November 30, 2015, it rendered Administrative Judgment (2015) Xi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 00267, dismissing Xixia's claims. The court acceptance fee for the first instance was RMB 50, to be borne by Xixia.

Dissatisfied with the first instance judgment, Xixia appealed to the Shaanxi High People's Court.

The facts found by the court of second instance were consistent with those found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that the Yulin Bureau's handling of the patent infringement dispute was based on Article 60 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 81 of the Implementing Regulations of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China. The deployment of administrative enforcement personnel within the system constitutes an internal act of the administrative organ and does not violate the internal exchange system. Given the shortage of existing staff, the Yulin Bureau, after seeking instructions from the Shaanxi Intellectual Property Office, seconded staff from the Baoji Intellectual Property Office to participate in the case. Moreover, during the oral hearing, the composition of the collegial panel was disclosed to the parties, and Xixia raised no objection. Therefore, the issuance of the administrative decision did not violate legal procedures. The sealed kiln body of the patent in suit and the jackets of the accused infringing device, as well as the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit and the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing device, did not constitute equivalent features. The administrative decision finding that Tianyuan did not infringe the patent was based on clear facts, conclusive evidence, and correct application of law. On June 6, 2016, the court of second instance rendered Administrative Judgment (2016) Shan Xing Zhong Zi No. 94, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. The court acceptance fee for the second instance was RMB 50, to be borne by Xixia.

Dissatisfied with the second instance judgment, Xixia applied to this Court for retrial, alleging: (1) The issuance of the administrative decision violated legal procedures. A. Patent administrative processing matters within the jurisdiction of the Yulin Bureau should be handled by staff of the Yulin Bureau. During his tenure as Deputy Director of the Baoji Intellectual Property Office, Gou Hongdong should not have served as the presiding examiner in hearing the patent infringement dispute. Although during the administrative litigation stage, the Yulin Bureau claimed it had obtained oral approval from the Shaanxi Intellectual Property Office and a reply letter from the Patent Administration Department of the China National Intellectual Property Administration, this still could not prove the legality of Gou Hongdong's participation in the collegial panel. B. During the second oral hearing of the Yulin Bureau, the parties were informed that Ai Long, a member of the collegial panel, had been replaced by Feng Xueliang, and Feng Xueliang participated in that oral hearing. However, the name signed on the administrative decision was Ai Long, not Feng Xueliang. This situation of "the adjudicator not hearing, the hearer not adjudicating" seriously affected the credibility and fairness of the administrative decision. (2) The administrative decision and the first and second instance judgments erroneously found that the accused infringing device did not fall within the scope of patent protection. A. The coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit and the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing device are identical technical features. The second instance judgment held that the sealed kiln body of the patent in suit was a complete spatial structure capable of containing other objects, and that the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe was a round, slender, and hollow structure. However, Claim 1 does not limit these specific shapes. The coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit and the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing device both essentially provide a channel for the movement and decomposition of coal material. The second instance judgment's finding that the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit had the effect of preventing heat loss and improving heat transfer efficiency, and that the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing device had the effect of reducing the risk of explosion, were both without basis. B. The sealed kiln body of the patent in suit and the jackets of the accused infringing device are equivalent technical features. In terms of means, both provide an enclosed cavity for high-temperature heating gas. The only difference is that the accused infringing device divides this cavity into three adjacent cavities, but there is no substantive difference in achieving the function of heating the object being heated. In terms of effect, although there may be slight differences in heating uniformity between the integral heating cavity and the three-section heating cavity, such differences would be readily conceivable by a person of ordinary skill in the art. Moreover, the patent specification does not involve improvements in heat exchange efficiency of the heat source. Any difference in heat exchange efficiency between the accused infringing device and the patent in suit is irrelevant to this case, and the comparison of heat exchange efficiency lacks evaluation standards and factual basis. Whether the jacket of the accused infringing device can rotate relative to the kiln body and how it rotates should not be the basis for evaluating whether the sealed kiln body and the jacket are identical. Furthermore, since all parties have no dispute that other technical features of Claim 1 are identical to the corresponding technical features of the accused infringing device, the accused infringing device falls within the scope of patent protection. In summary, the first and second instance judgments and the administrative decision erroneously applied the law, lacked evidentiary support for key factual findings, and violated procedures. Pursuant to Items 3, 4, and 5 of Article 91 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Xixia requests this Court to retry the case, revoke the administrative decision and the first and second instance judgments, and order the Yulin Bureau to render a new administrative decision.

The Yulin Bureau submitted its opinion, stating: (1) The issuance of the administrative decision complied with legal provisions. A. The patent infringement dispute was a cross-provincial, significant, complex, and influential case. After seeking instructions, the Shaanxi Intellectual Property Office decided to deploy personnel to participate in the collegial panel, and this was approved by a letter from the China National Intellectual Property Administration. All members of the collegial panel held enforcement certificates and had enforcement qualifications. During the first oral hearing, the Yulin Bureau informed the parties of the composition of the collegial panel and specifically explained the reasons for Gou Hongdong and Bai Long's participation. Xixia raised no objection and expressly stated it would not file a recusal request. Even if there were defects in the composition of the collegial panel in the administrative processing procedure, it did not substantially affect Xixia's rights. This falls under the circumstance of Item 2 of Article 74 of the Administrative Procedure Law, where the administrative act need not be revoked. B. During the second oral hearing, Ai Long was replaced by Feng Xueliang due to temporary business. However, Ai Long participated in the first oral hearing, and considering he was the Deputy Director of the Yulin Bureau, it was not improper for Ai Long to sign the administrative decision. (2) The administrative decision finding that Tianyuan did not infringe the patent was not erroneous. When the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit is simplified to one, the protected structure becomes a double-layer jacket structure, with the core structure being an outer tubular sealed kiln body into which heating gas is introduced. This is no different from rotary kilns already used in industry. Traditional rotary kiln structures are equipment for heating and dry-distilling large lump coal in a pipe, but they cannot be used for pulverized coal, which the patent in suit aims to process. Therefore, the patent in suit employs multiple evenly arranged coal material propulsion decomposition pipes to increase the heating area of pulverized coal and improve pyrolysis efficiency. As described in the specification and drawings, the inventive point of the patent in suit lies in the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe composed of multiple densely arranged parallel pipes, whereas the accused infringing device has only a single rotary kiln body for coal material decomposition. Even if the patent structure is changed to two cylinders, the outer cylinder remains a closed structure, which is different from the three-section non-closed structure of the accused infringing device. The jacket of the accused infringing device and the sealed kiln body of the patent in suit, as well as the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing device and the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit, differ in positional relationship, installation structure, working principle, technical effect, and purpose, and do not constitute identical or equivalent features.

Tianyuan submitted its opinion, stating: (1) During the oral hearing, the Yulin Bureau informed the parties of the composition of the collegial panel, and Xixia raised no objection. Although Ai Long did not participate in the second oral hearing, he participated in the first oral hearing. Therefore, his signing of the administrative decision did not violate legal procedures. (2) The jacket of the accused infringing device is not equivalent to the sealed kiln body of the patent in suit. The jacket of the accused infringing device is merely a heating sleeve on part of the outer wall of the rotary kiln, without a sealed structure. The overall structure of the rotary kiln is much larger than the jacket and rotates relative to it. Its rotational transmission structure cannot be placed in a high-temperature environment, and the rotary kiln cannot be arranged inside the jacket. Although Claim 1 of the patent in suit defines coal inlets and outlets on the pipe, since the pipe is inside the sealed kiln body, it is actually impossible to have coal inlets and outlets on the pipe. The jacket of the accused infringing device has no coal inlets or outlets. The heat exchange chamber of the patent in suit is formed inside the sealed kiln body between the inner wall of the kiln and the coal material decomposition propulsion pipe, whereas the jacket heat exchange space of the accused infringing device only partially covers the outer wall of the rotary kiln and cannot be completely sealed. Thus, there is a large temperature gradient and low thermal utilization efficiency. However, the jacket completely eliminates the risk of hot air contacting pyrolysis gas inside the kiln, providing higher safety. Therefore, the accused infringing device does not fall within the scope of patent protection, and the administrative decision should be upheld.

This Court finds during the retrial that the facts found by the courts of first and second instance are substantially correct.

During the trial before this Court, all parties confirmed the following: 1. No party objected to the characterization of the features of the patent in suit and the accused infringing device in the administrative decision and the first and second instance judgments. The disputed technical features are: whether the jackets of the accused infringing device are equivalent to the sealed kiln body of the patent in suit, and whether the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing device is equivalent to the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit. 2. Coal material is directly loaded into both the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe of the patent in suit and the rotary kiln body of the accused infringing device. 3. Each jacket of the accused infringing device and the pipe form a sealed heat exchange chamber. 4. The total length of the coal pipe of the accused infringing device is approximately 35 meters, with a gap of approximately 2 meters between two jackets. 5. During the oral hearing before the Yulin Bureau, Tianyuan expressly stated it did not assert the prior art defense. 6. The Patent Administrative Enforcement Certificate indicates that the enforcement territory is the administrative division of the certificate holder's work unit.

It is further found that, during his tenure as a member of the collegial panel of the administrative decision, Gou Hongdong was a staff member of the Baoji Intellectual Property Office. There was no formal official document deciding to transfer him to participate in the administrative processing of the dispute. The oral hearing records of the Yulin Bureau do not reflect that Xixia or Tianyuan were informed of Gou Hongdong's official status or the reasons for his participation in the collegial panel. The Yulin Bureau conducted two oral hearings for the patent infringement dispute. During the second oral hearing, Xixia and Tianyuan were informed that Ai Long, a member of the collegial panel, had been replaced by Feng Xueliang. The administrative decision was signed by Gou Hongdong as the presiding examiner, and by Ai Long, Zhang Weiliang, Bai Long, and He Xiaojuan as examiners.

The above facts are supported by the trial records, the Yulin Bureau's oral hearing records, and other evidence.

This Court holds that the issues in dispute are: 1. Whether the issuance of the administrative decision violated legal procedures. 2. Whether the administrative decision and the first and second instance judgments erroneously applied the law.

Regarding the first issue, this Court holds that the issuance of the administrative decision violated legal procedures and should be revoked. The specific reasoning is as follows:

First, in adjudicating the patent infringement dispute between two equal civil parties, Xixia and Tianyuan, the Yulin Bureau, upon Xixia's request, determined whether Tianyuan had infringed the patent. It was essentially in a position of adjudicating a dispute. The determination of patent infringement concerns the delineation of the scope of patent rights, involves the significant interests of the parties, and relates to scientific and technological innovation and economic and social development. It requires strict and standardized dispute resolution procedures. When handling the patent infringement dispute, the Yulin Bureau should have adhered to the procedural principles of rigor, standardization, openness, and equality. However, after Ai Long had been explicitly replaced by Feng Xueliang, Ai Long's name was nevertheless signed on the administrative decision. This effectively constituted "the adjudicator not hearing, the hearer not adjudicating." Such a situation deviates from the tenet of law-based administration and diminishes public trust in administrative enforcement entities. The fact that the case could not be resolved even after being heard by intermediate and high courts is mainly due to this reason. Regarding such significant and fundamental procedural matters, the Yulin Bureau failed to exercise due and sufficient caution and attention. Its error in this regard itself constitutes a serious and obvious violation of legal procedures, and clearly does not fall within the category of "minor procedural violations of an administrative act that do not require revocation" as asserted by the Yulin Bureau.

Second, the administrative act in this case is the Yulin Bureau's administrative handling of the patent infringement dispute. This administrative handling was made in the name of the Yulin Bureau and implemented by a five-member collegial panel. That administrative enforcement personnel possess corresponding enforcement qualifications is a necessary requirement for the legality of the administrative subject's qualification and an inevitable requirement for comprehensively advancing law-based administration. In principle, the collegial panel of the Yulin Bureau that made the administrative decision should consist of staff members of that bureau who have patent administrative enforcement qualifications. All parties confirmed that the Patent Administrative Enforcement Certificate indicates that the enforcement territory is the administrative division of the certificate holder's work unit, which corroborates the above conclusion. Even if, as the Yulin Bureau claims, it had a short establishment history, insufficient enforcement personnel, and lacked experience, necessitating the deployment of experienced enforcement personnel from other regions to participate in case hearings, this does not mean that the situation of "the adjudicator not hearing, the hearer not adjudicating" is permissible. Nor does it mean that the deployment of enforcement personnel can be done without fulfilling formal and complete official document procedures. Otherwise, the standardization and seriousness of administrative enforcement procedures cannot be guaranteed. This would be detrimental to regulating administrative enforcement activities and to strengthening administrative enforcement responsibilities. However, the Yulin Bureau did not submit any formal official document for the transfer of Gou Hongdong to participate in handling the dispute. The so-called reply (photocopy) of the Coordination and Protection Office of the Shaanxi Intellectual Property Office submitted in the first instance was actually an internal request from that office to the leadership of the Shaanxi Intellectual Property Office. It had no document number and no official seal, and was overly simple and casual. This Court does not recognize this material as a lawful and valid basis for Gou Hongdong's participation in the collegial panel of the administrative decision. As for the Reply on Deploying Enforcement Personnel in Individual Cases issued by the Patent Administration Department of the China National Intellectual Property Administration to the Shaanxi Intellectual Property Office, formally, this reply was made on November 20, 2015, after the issuance of the administrative decision. Substantively, this reply states that the deployment of enforcement personnel does not violate the relevant provisions on civil service exchanges. This has no direct relevance to the dispute in this case concerning whether the procedures for the transfer of enforcement personnel were formal and complete. Therefore, this reply also cannot serve as a basis for the lawful participation of Gou Hongdong in the collegial panel of the administrative decision.

Third, strengthening judicial supervision over administrative enforcement of intellectual property rights, and vigorously regulating and promoting law-based administration by administrative organs, are important manifestations of the leading role of judicial protection of intellectual property rights. They are also important elements in strengthening the rule of law in the field of intellectual property rights, and are of great significance for optimizing the legal environment for scientific and technological innovation. In this case, although the Yulin Bureau claims that during the oral hearing it informed the parties of Gou Hongdong's specific status and the reasons for his participation in the collegial panel, the evidence it submitted cannot prove this assertion. Therefore, whether Xixia accepted the identity of the collegial panel members is neither a prerequisite nor a requirement for this Court to evaluate the procedural legality of the administrative act. It is particularly important to point out that the replacement of Ai Long by Feng Xueliang, followed by Ai Long's signing of the administrative decision, already constitutes a serious violation of legal procedures. This is not affected by the subjective perception of the administrative counterpart, nor is it changed by the fact that the administrative counterpart did not raise an objection. Xixia's raising of this issue and its request in the retrial are not improper. Therefore, this Court does not support the arguments of the Yulin Bureau and Tianyuan that "the procedure is legal because Xixia did not object to the composition of the collegial panel."

Regarding the second issue, this Court holds that the administrative decision and the first and second instance judgments erroneously applied the law and should be corrected. The specific reasoning is as follows:

(I) Interpretation of the sealed kiln body of the patent in suit

The administrative decision held that, according to the description in paragraph 0021 of the patent specification and the working principle, the sealed kiln body of the patent in suit is fixed relative to the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe, rotating by itself and driving the internal coal material propulsion decomposition pipe to rotate. In contrast, the jacket of the accused infringing device itself does not rotate, and the rotary kiln body it encloses rotates relative to the jacket. Therefore, the structures, functions, and effects of the two are different. In response, this Court holds that, pursuant to Article 59 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, the scope of protection of an invention or utility model patent shall be determined by the content of the claims. The description and drawings may be used to interpret the claims. It can be seen that the content of the claims is the sole criterion for delineating the scope of patent protection, and the description and drawings are only used to interpret the content of the claims. Therefore, when using the description and drawings to interpret the claims, one cannot read the specific descriptions of specific embodiments from the description into the claims. Otherwise, the scope of patent protection would be unreasonably narrowed. Claim 1 of the patent in suit does not limit whether the sealed kiln body and the coal material propulsion decomposition pipe rotate. Paragraph 0021 of the patent specification is a specific implementation of the patented technical solution. The description of the rotary kiln body in this paragraph should not be used to limit the sealed kiln body of Claim 1. That is, whether the kiln body of the accused infringing device rotates does not affect the determination of patent infringement in this case.

The Disputed Administrative Decision also held that, in order to improve heat utilization efficiency and pyrolysis efficiency, the sealed kiln body of the Patent-in-Suit required the heat exchange chamber to be a continuous space, whereas the heat exchange chamber of the Alleged Infringing Device consisted of three discontinuous spaces formed between three jackets and the kiln body for the convenience of equipment manufacturing and the safety of the pyrolysis process, with differences in structure, effect, and purpose. In this regard, this Court holds that the kiln body of the Alleged Infringing Device is wrapped in segments by three jackets, forming three sealed heat exchange spaces respectively, the main function of which is to heat the coal material inside the pipeline, which is also the technical function to be achieved by the Patent-in-Suit. Although the three-section heating cavity of the Alleged Infringing Device has certain differences in heating effect compared with the integrated heating cavity of the Patent-in-Suit, all parties confirmed that "the total length of the coal pipeline of the Alleged Infringing Device is approximately 35 meters, and the gap between two jackets is approximately 2 meters." Generally speaking, a gap of about one-tenth of the coal pipeline should not cause a substantial change in the overall heating function and effect of the coal pipeline. In this regard, Tianyuan Company did not adduce evidence to prove that the heat exchange efficiency of its device was significantly lower than that of the technical solution of the Patent-in-Suit. As for the claim of the Disputed Administrative Decision and Tianyuan Company concerning the improvement of safety of the pyrolysis process by the Alleged Infringing Device, there is also no relevant evidence on record to support it.

Therefore, the interpretation of the sealed kiln body of the Patent-in-Suit in the Disputed Administrative Decision is erroneous.

(II) Interpretation of the Coal Material Propulsion and Decomposition Pipeline of the Patent-in-Suit

The Disputed Administrative Decision held that the coal material propulsion and decomposition pipeline of the Patent-in-Suit was fixed inside the sealed kiln body, whereas the rotary kiln body of the Alleged Infringing Device rotated relative to the jackets, with differences in structure and working principle. In this regard, this Court holds that, as stated above, claim 1 of the Patent-in-Suit does not limit whether the coal material propulsion and decomposition pipeline rotates; whether the kiln body of the Alleged Infringing Device rotates does not affect the determination of patent infringement in this case.

Yulin Bureau further argued in the retrial before this Court that, as described in Paragraph [0023] of the specification and the accompanying drawings, the invention point of the Patent-in-Suit was to adopt a coal material propulsion and decomposition pipeline composed of multiple densely arranged parallel pipes, whereas the coal material decomposition pipeline of the Alleged Infringing Device had only one rotary kiln body. In this regard, this Court holds that claim 1 of the Patent-in-Suit does not further limit the number and position of the coal material propulsion and decomposition pipeline; on the contrary, its dependent claim 5 states: "The inner-coal outer-heat type coal material decomposition device as claimed in claim 1 or 2, characterized in that: the coal material propulsion and decomposition pipeline is composed of a plurality of densely arranged parallel pipes, one end of the plurality of densely arranged parallel pipes is provided with a distribution disk, the distribution disk is communicated with the coal inlet, and the other end is provided with a collection disk, the collection disk is communicated with the coal outlet." According to the rules for drafting claims stipulated in the Rules for the Implementation of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, a dependent claim is a further limitation of the independent claim from which it depends, and the scope of protection of an independent claim shall be larger than that of its dependent claims. Therefore, according to the limitation in claim 5 that "the coal material propulsion and decomposition pipeline is composed of a plurality of densely arranged parallel pipes," it can be inferred that the coal material propulsion and decomposition pipeline of claim 1, from which it depends, does not require multiple densely arranged parallel pipes. Moreover, as confirmed by the parties, "coal material is directly loaded into both the coal material propulsion and decomposition pipeline of the Patent-in-Suit and the rotary kiln body of the Alleged Infringing Device," it can be known that regardless of the specific name of the device in which coal material is directly loaded in the Alleged Infringing Device, there is no substantial difference in means, function, and effect compared with the coal material propulsion and decomposition pipeline of the Patent-in-Suit.

Therefore, the interpretation of the coal material propulsion and decomposition pipeline of the Patent-in-Suit in the Disputed Administrative Decision is erroneous.

In summary, the Disputed Administrative Decision violated legal procedures and applied the law erroneously; the judgments of the first and second instances also erred in their findings on the substantive and procedural issues in dispute, and should be revoked together in accordance with the law. Based on the actual conditions of the current patent legal system in China, the patent infringement dispute between Xixia Company and Tianyuan Company can be resolved more effectively and practically through civil litigation. For the purpose of facilitating acceptance and ending the dispute, this Court explained to Xixia Company and inquired whether it would choose to file a civil lawsuit separately with a People's Court regarding the patent infringement dispute. Xixia Company submitted a written opinion to this Court, insisting that Yulin Bureau make a new administrative decision in accordance with the law.

Separately, on December 15, 2017, Tianyuan Company submitted a written application to this Court stating that the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office had accepted a request for invalidation declaration against the Patent-in-Suit, the patent rights were in an unstable state, and the determination of patent infringement required the patent to be valid as a prerequisite, requesting this Court to suspend the proceedings. In this regard, this Court holds that the utility model patent evaluation report submitted by Xixia Company during the administrative proceedings showed that no defects that would not meet the conditions for granting patent rights were found in all claims of the Patent-in-Suit. Currently, the patent rights of the Patent-in-Suit remain valid. The acceptance by the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office of the request for invalidation declaration against the Patent-in-Suit is not a circumstance that necessitates the suspension of the proceedings. Therefore, the request of Tianyuan Company to suspend the proceedings in this case is not supported.

Pursuant to Item (2) and Item (3) of Article 70, Item (2) of Paragraph 1 of Article 89 and Paragraph 3 of Article 89 of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Paragraph 1 of Article 76 and Article 78 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Implementation of the Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Revoke the Administrative Judgment (2016) Shaan Xing Zhong Zi No. 94 of the Shaanxi High People's Court;

2. Revoke the Administrative Judgment (2015) Xi Zhong Xing Chu Zi No. 00267 of the Xi'an Intermediate People's Court, Shaanxi Province;

3. Revoke the Patent Infringement Dispute Handling Decision Yu Zhi Fa Chu Zi [2015] No. 9 of Yulin Municipal Intellectual Property Office;

4. Order Yulin Municipal Intellectual Property Office to make a new administrative decision.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of 50 yuan and the second-instance case acceptance fee of 50 yuan shall be borne by Yulin Municipal Intellectual Property Office.

This judgment is final.
